html:
Navaho marks the Navajo people in the 1500s, in the high country of northwest New Mexico, the region they call Dinétah. They were then a fairly new people in the Southwest, speaking a Southern Athabaskan language close to that of the Apache.

They hunted, gathered and farmed maize learned from their Pueblo neighbours, and traded with them for cloth and pottery. Spanish records first name them in the early 1600s as the "Apaches de Nabajó", the Apaches of the farm fields. After Juan de Oñate set up the colony of New Mexico in 1598, the Navajo began to raid for horses and sheep. Those animals changed their lives, and within a century they had become herders and weavers. After the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, Pueblo refugees joining them added to Navajo ways.
